base.pair_handling.score_rubric_note: No anchor-9 clause names the deviation. Anchor 10's canonical clause fails for the three caching classes. For xcorr, coint and je the kept A[i,j] is the cached bivariate(j, i) value, so upper-only runs differ by up to 0.081 (xcorr) and 7.41 (coint_aeg). The supplement's 'repeated entries' sentence holds (max|A - A.T| = 0 on 15 mirror classes). The developer-guide triangle mismatch the record also cites is GitBook text, which anchor 10 does not name.

basic.cov.EllipticEnvelope.score_rubric_note: Anchor 6: sklearn 1.9.1 reweighted FAST-MCD, bitwise equal to cov_MinCovDet under the same RNG state (eeqmcd 8/8). From the same raw h-subset robustbase agrees to 3.5e-15 (rdet 5/6; the sixth differs by one reweighting point, 0.0118). It differs from canonical MCD (RNG-dependent h-subset, h = ceil, MLE divisor) and from the supplement (values up to 1.141, so not a correlation).

basic.cov.EmpiricalCovariance.score_rubric_note: Anchor-9 ddof clause. The MLE covariance agrees with the numpy reference to 1.22e-15. The gap to the supplement's 'equivalent to correlation' is the factor (T-1)/T from ddof=1 z-scoring (0.984375 at T=64).

basic.cov.GraphicalLasso.score_rubric_note: Anchors 8 and 9 do not fit. The record gives no constant-factor relationship to Friedman 2008, and the author package (R glasso) agrees on only 10/11 runs: on var2_bivariate T4096 the solver returns its 0.95*S start, 8.65e-4 from the optimum. The row sits at anchor 7's optimiser clause. That clause holds on well-conditioned inputs (ADMM 17/17 within 5.64e-5) but not on every input (KKT 34/37; trending T4096 raises FloatingPointError).

basic.cov.GraphicalLassoCV.score_rubric_note: Anchor 6: sklearn's approximate, silent optimisation at the CV-selected alpha_ deviates from the canonical graphical lasso, and the value is not the documented correlation. Anchor 7's optimality clause fails: KKT passes 32/37, 17 of 35 refits did not converge, the P=2 closed form is off by 7.06e-3 on logistic_maps_bidir T1024, and three inputs give all-NaN output. An independent re-scoring of the CV folds selects the same alpha_ on 6/6 runs.

basic.cov.LedoitWolf.score_rubric_note: Anchor 10's supplement clause fails. The supplement says covariance equals correlation, but pyspi/r = (1-s)(T-1)/T = 0.8030 at T=64 (doc-corr max rel 0.197). No anchor-9 clause names the shrinkage factor. The estimate agrees with the independent LW 2004 reference to 3.67e-15.

basic.cov.MinCovDet.score_rubric_note: Anchor 6: sklearn 1.9.1 reweighted FAST-MCD. From the same raw h-subset robustbase agrees to 3.5e-15 (rdet 7/8; the eighth differs by one reweighting point, 0.0118). It differs from canonical MCD: the h-subset depends on the RNG and is the best found in only 3/14 runs, h = ceil, and the divisor is MLE. It differs from the supplement because values reach 1.141, so it is not a correlation.

basic.cov.OAS.score_rubric_note: Anchor 8 does not fit: the no-2/p shrinkage is 14.4% above Chen et al. Eq. 23 at p=4 and moves off-diagonals by up to 2.9% (p=4, T=64). Anchor 7 holds only in part. pyspi equals an independent numpy kernel of the no-2/p formula, which sklearn 0.24.1 (the version the supplement names) also computes (35/35 value runs, max abs 1.22e-15). The supplement's 'covariance equals correlation' sentence does not hold, because the value is (1-s)(T-1)/T r. The same sentence keeps LedoitWolf and ShrunkCovariance off 10.

basic.cov.ShrunkCovariance.score_rubric_note: Anchor 10's supplement clause fails. The supplement names this fixed-0.1 estimator but also says covariance equals correlation; pyspi/r = 0.9(T-1)/T = 0.8859 at T=64 (doc-corr max rel 0.114). The estimate agrees with the independent reference to 1.11e-15.

basic.kendalltau.score_rubric_note: Tau-b equals a from-scratch Kendall 1945 kernel and R stats::cor to max_abs 1.7e-16 over 38 exact runs, as the supplement's 'kendalltau in SciPy' text states. The Kendall 1938 (tau-a) citation and the 'linear' class label are metadata conflicts.

basic.prec.EllipticEnvelope.score_rubric_note: Deviates from canonical MCD (global-RNG FAST-MCD starts, ceil h, MLE divisor) and from the supplement (raw precision -2.480 vs documented partial correlation +0.8). Given the same raw subset it agrees with robustbase to max_rel 1.76e-14 (rdet 5/6).

basic.prec.EmpiricalCovariance.score_rubric_note: Anchor 10's second clause fails. The supplement calls the value the partial correlation in [-1, 1], but pyspi returns the raw precision entry (bivariate_gaussian T=1024 pair (2,3): -2.193 vs partial correlation +0.797; up to 95.3 on cointegrated). The numeric clause holds: the independent reference (LU inverse; a pseudo-inverse on the singular and average-referenced inputs) agrees on 36/36 value runs, max abs 1.3e-11, max rel 1e-9.

basic.prec.GraphicalLasso.score_rubric_note: Anchor 7's optimality clause fails: the KKT residual on Theta is <= 1e-4 in only 16/37 runs (0.212 on shared_envelope T=1024). The raw precision entry has the opposite sign to the documented partial correlation on 100% of nonzero entries.

basic.prec.GraphicalLassoCV.score_rubric_note: Anchor 7's optimality clause fails: the KKT residual on Theta is <= 1e-4 in only 16/37 runs (narrowband up to 0.232). The raw precision entry has the opposite sign to the documented partial correlation on 83-100% of nonzero entries.

basic.prec.LedoitWolf.score_rubric_note: Anchor 10's second clause fails. The supplement calls the value the partial correlation in [-1, 1], but pyspi returns the raw precision entry (bivariate_gaussian T=1024 pair (2,3): -2.061 vs partial correlation +0.786; up to 61.5 on cointegrated). The numeric clause holds: the LU inverse of a from-scratch Ledoit-Wolf estimate agrees on 36/36 runs, max abs 4.28e-12, max rel 1.6e-11.

basic.prec.MinCovDet.score_rubric_note: Deviates from canonical MCD (global-RNG starts with a 20-seed spread of 0.817 at T=64, ceil h, MLE divisor) and from the supplement (-2.480 vs documented partial correlation +0.8). Given the raw subset, the arithmetic agrees to max_rel 1.54e-13 (state 18/18).

basic.prec.OAS.score_rubric_note: Deviates from both. It inverts sklearn's no-2/p OAS (off-diagonal gap to the Chen et al. Eq. 23 inverse: median 5.1%, max 12.7% at p=4 T=64), and the raw precision entry has the opposite sign to the documented partial correlation (-2.057 vs +0.786).

basic.prec.ShrunkCovariance.score_rubric_note: Anchor 10's second clause fails. The supplement calls the value the partial correlation in [-1, 1], but pyspi returns the raw precision entry (bivariate_gaussian T=1024 pair (2,3): -1.482 vs partial correlation +0.717; up to 4.258 on cointegrated). The numeric clause holds: the LU inverse of 0.9 S + 0.1 tr(S)/p I agrees on 36/36 runs, max abs 3.02e-14, max rel 1.13e-11.

basic.spearmanr.score_rubric_note: The Pearson correlation of mid-ranks equals a from-scratch kernel and R stats::cor to max_abs 2.2e-16 over 38 exact runs, as the supplement's 'spearmanr in SciPy' text states. Only metadata disagrees: the 'linear' class label vs the 'nonlinear' keyword, the double 'signed'/'unsigned' labels (bug 4) and the undocumented spearmanr-sq.

basic.xcorr.max_sig-False.score_rubric_note: Anchor 9 fails: the T/(T-1) factor is not a documented convention, and identical series give 1.0159 at T=64 against the documented [-1, 1]. Anchor 8's monotone clause also fails on the constructed end-lag pair (0.7596 vs 0.1054 by channel order at T=1024, canonical 0.7589 in both orders). Every dataset pipeline run equals the canonical maximum times T/(T-1) to <= 6.7e-16, so the row sits at 8.

basic.xcorr.max_sig-True.score_rubric_note: It is the maximum over a window set by a doubled threshold, a lag +1 centre and a mirrored left cut. The documented reading agrees on 0/20 runs. Channel order moves delayed_noise A[0,3] from 0.081 to 0.993.

basic.xcorr.mean_sig-False.score_rubric_note: The constant factor T/(T-1) plus the one-lag-shifted window account for the whole gap (gap_d2 <= 6.1e-18 once both are applied). The shift changes the value (relative gap_d0 up to 0.54), so anchor 8 fails.

basic.xcorr.mean_sig-True.score_rubric_note: The kept window averages about T//4 mostly insignificant lags (at most 0.39% significant at T=1024), so 'sig-True' does not describe the computation. The rho=0.8 pair scores 0.0010.

causal.anm.score_rubric_note: Anchor 4: the GP has no noise term and interpolates (std(r)/std(y) <= 1.3e-9 in 7/7 collapse runs), so the score is m*HSIC_b of x and (K + alpha I)^-1 y, a near-symmetric dependence score. It is within the raw-pair tolerance (median rel < 0.1, max < 0.3) of plain m*HSIC_b(x, y) in 10 of 13 runs. The replica at sklearn's theta agrees to <= 1.6e-15 on 8 of 9 runs.

causal.ccm.E-1.score_rubric_note: Anchor 6: the kernel agrees with an independent simplex cross-map to max_abs 1.65e-14. The curve has 22 library sizes, not the supplement's 21, and stops at 52 of 60 at T=64. Mean/max replace the convergence test, and rows are targets.

causal.ccm.E-10.score_rubric_note: Anchor 6: the kernel agrees with an independent simplex cross-map to max_abs 1.94e-14. The curve has 22 library sizes, not the supplement's 21, and stops short at T=256 (20..230 of 20..240). Mean/max replace the convergence test, and rows are targets.

causal.ccm.E-None.score_rubric_note: Anchor 4 names CCM max-E selection: pyspi passes E = 10 for every process (known bug 2), and ccm_E-None_* equals ccm_E-10_* bitwise. At the documented E = 2 on chaotic T=256, the reference gives A[1,0] 0.687 vs A[0,1] 0.199; pyspi gives 0.281 vs 0.284.

causal.cds.score_rubric_note: Anchor 6: 23/23 exact runs reproduce cdt's formula (max abs 2.8e-17). That formula departs from Fonollosa's stated parameters (max rel 0.36-0.58) and from the supplement's 'SD of y given x' wording.

causal.igci.score_rubric_note: Anchor 10's first clause fails: pyspi returns -C_{i->j} (cdt sign), equal to a sign-flipped Daniusis eq. (12) reference to max abs 3.0e-14 in 22/22 runs. Anchor 9 names the sign of a symmetric quantity. igci is antisymmetric (max|A + A.T| = 0.0), and its sign is documented only in cdt's docstring. So 9 is the highest anchor cleared, by analogy.

causal.reci.score_rubric_note: Anchor 7: 24/24 exact runs agree with a numpy OLS on [1, x^3] after [0, 1] min-max scaling, the supplement's cubic-plus-constant MSE (max abs 5.6e-17). Canonical RECI differs: it uses a selected function class and held-out MSE.

distance.bary.dtw.score_rubric_note: Anchor 7, first clause: pyspi runs the DBA the supplement names, and the from-scratch DBA reproduces it (52/52 runs, max_rel 4.2e-14). It differs from the canonical Frechet mean: one mean-initialised run has a cost a relative 0.12-0.56 (bivariate_gaussian) and 1.85-44.5 (delayed_noise) above the best of 8 starts.

distance.bary.euclidean.score_rubric_note: The representative bary_euclidean_mean is identically 0 on z-scored input: max|A| 2.52e-16 over 84 runs.

distance.bary.sgddtw.score_rubric_note: Anchor 5, second clause: the from-scratch SSG reproduces pyspi (33/33 runs, max_abs 2.2e-16). SSG with last-sample early stopping has no literature definition, and it stops after 3-5 epochs on Gaussian pairs.

distance.bary.softdtw.score_rubric_note: Anchor 7's optimiser clause fails: optimality fails on 7 of 10 runs (relative gap up to 0.0138 at T=64). tslearn returns res.x at tol 1e-3, which departs from both the supplement's 'minimizes' and the canonical argmin.

distance.dcorr.biased-False.score_rubric_note: Anchor 9 squared-vs-not: the SPI returns the bias-corrected dCor^2 (R*_n), matching dcor u_distance_correlation_sqr to <= 7.2e-14 in 8/8 runs, while the sqrt form is 0.067-0.250 away.

distance.dcorr.biased-True.score_rubric_note: Anchor 9 squared-vs-not: returns unsquared dCor_n (dcor distance_correlation to <= 9.4e-14, 8/8 runs) while sibling dcorr is on the dCor^2 scale, a split the supplement does not state.

distance.dcorrx.maxlag-1.score_rubric_note: Anchor 3 names mgcx lag handling, which dcorrx shares: the lag-1 term is dCor^2 of distance-profile rows, and the total differs from the series-slice statistic by up to 0.0794 (gauss_ar1_pair).

distance.dcorrx.maxlag-10.score_rubric_note: Anchor 3 names mgcx lag handling, which dcorrx shares: lag terms 1..10 are dCor^2 of distance-profile rows; total 7.116 vs series-slice 5.899 on narrowband_f0-0.25 T256 pair (2,0).

distance.dtw.constraint-None.score_rubric_note: Equal to the tslearn form the supplement names: 16/16 dp runs bit-identical, and dtaidistance gives max_abs 0.0. The Sakoe-Chiba 1978 form differs by a ratio of 23.96-55.18, with Spearman 0.77-0.96.

distance.dtw.constraint-itakura.score_rubric_note: 16/16 dp runs are bit-identical to the masked from-scratch DP. The 1978 form differs by a ratio of 25.6-62.2, with Spearman 0.71-0.95.

distance.dtw.constraint-sakoe_chiba.score_rubric_note: A radius fixed at 1 sample blocks the documented shifting. Delays of 3 and 5 keep dtw/||z0-zk|| at 0.724/0.731, against 0.098/0.123 under itakura (delayed_noise T1024).

distance.gwtau.score_rubric_note: Anchor 8 names a constant factor such as T/(T-1): pyspi leaves the root out of the uniform measure, so pyspi = canonical * sqrt(T/(T-1)) (0.79 % at T=64, 0.012 % at T=4096). The authors' MATLAB code does the same.

distance.hhg.score_rubric_note: On continuous data pyspi is bit-identical to the from-scratch Heller et al. statistic (14 def runs, max_abs 0.0). Tie rounding on tied data (up to 4.9e-2 relative, raw logistic_maps T=256) sits under anchor 9's estimator-variance clause. Anchor 10 fails because the supplement describes an RKHS kernel statistic on ranks of the variables.

distance.hsic.biased-False.score_rubric_note: Anchor 6: returns HSIC_u normalised by its self-terms with the x-only median bandwidth, 8.4-18.8x raw HSIC_u; neither the normalisation nor the bandwidth rule is in the supplement.

distance.hsic.biased-True.score_rubric_note: Anchor 6: returns sqrt of normalised HSIC_b with the x-only median bandwidth (0.18913 stored vs raw HSIC_b 0.00276 on bivariate_gaussian T1024); the supplement describes raw HSIC.

distance.lcss.constraint-None.score_rubric_note: Anchor 10's canonical clause fails only on exact ties: the match test is <= eps where Vlachos et al. use < eps (probe lcss([0,0],[1,1]) = 1.0 vs 0.0). On the audit data the two rules agree (3 strict-rule runs, max_abs 0.0) and 17/17 dp runs are bit-identical. No anchor-9 clause names a tie rule.

distance.lcss.constraint-itakura.score_rubric_note: The itakura mask is ignored, so pyspi equals unconstrained lcss bit for bit. On iid_gaussian T1024 pair (0,1) pyspi gives 0.8037 against 0.0 for the masked LCSS.

distance.lcss.constraint-sakoe_chiba.score_rubric_note: The band is ignored, so pyspi equals unconstrained lcss bit for bit. On iid_gaussian T1024 pair (0,1) pyspi gives 0.8037 against 0.7061 for the masked LCSS; the masked null test fails with max_z 8.2.

distance.mgc.score_rubric_note: SciPy's region rule matches neither the paper (2n) nor r-mgc and moves values by up to 0.061 at T=256. The global fallback is column-centred dCorr, not the supplement's unbiased estimator (differs by 1.79e-3 at T=64).

distance.mgcx.maxlag-1.score_rubric_note: Anchor 3 names mgcx lag handling: the lag-1 term is MGC of distance-profile rows; total 0.8163 vs series-slice 0.8904 on narrowband_f0-0.25 T256 pair (1,0).

distance.mgcx.maxlag-10.score_rubric_note: Anchor 3 names mgcx lag handling: lag terms 1..10 are MGC of distance-profile rows; total 4.0807 vs series-slice 4.8156 on narrowband_f0-0.25 T256 pair (1,0).

distance.pdist.braycurtis.score_rubric_note: Anchor 8 fails. SciPy's |x+y| denominator equals the canonical sum(x+y) only for non-negative data, so on z-scored input the value is not a constant factor or monotone map of the canonical [0,1] index and leaves that range (rho=-0.8 gives 3.054 at T=1024; y=-x gives +inf). Anchor 7's supplement-variant clause is met only through the GitBook sklearn braycurtis form (max_rel 5.28e-15), because the supplement does not mention pdist.

distance.pdist.canberra.score_rubric_note: Anchor 10's supplement clause fails because the supplement does not mention pdist. The record also holds its canonical clause short: pyspi reproduces the |x|+|y| form to max_rel 1.69e-15, but Lance and Williams defined the index for non-negative data, and on z-scored signed data y=-x gives exactly T (1024.0). No anchor-9 clause names this generalisation.

distance.pdist.chebyshev.score_rubric_note: Anchor 10's supplement clause fails because the supplement does not mention pdist. The numeric half holds: 14 from-definition kernel and pipeline runs are bit-identical (max_abs 0.0).
distance.pdist.chebyshev.score_adjustment_reason: R3: the supplement does not mention pdist, so the GitBook page (sklearn pairwise distances, metric chebyshev) is the documented definition, and pyspi agrees with it bit for bit in 14 from-definition runs.

distance.pdist.cityblock.score_rubric_note: Anchor 10's supplement clause fails because the supplement does not mention pdist. The numeric half holds: the from-definition reference agrees to max_rel 3.55e-15 in 15 runs.
distance.pdist.cityblock.score_adjustment_reason: R3: the supplement does not mention pdist, so the GitBook page (sklearn pairwise distances, metric cityblock) is the documented definition, and pyspi agrees with it to max_rel 3.55e-15 in 15 from-definition runs.

distance.pdist.cosine.score_rubric_note: Anchor 10's 1e-8 relative bar fails on near-identical rows. Against the cancellation-free form the relative error is 2.2e-6 at eps 1e-5 and 1.0 at eps 1e-9 (pyspi 0.0 vs 4.95e-19). The supplement also does not mention pdist.
distance.pdist.cosine.score_adjustment_reason: R2: max_abs 3.8e-16 <= 1e-12 and pyspi equals the canonical 1-S from definition to 4.4e-16; R3: GitBook names sklearn pairwise_distances cosine, reproduced to 8.9e-16

distance.pdist.euclidean.score_rubric_note: Anchor 10's 1e-8 relative bar fails. sklearn's dot-product expansion returns 1.19e-7 to 9.54e-7 instead of 0 for a duplicated channel (3 of 4 dup runs fail) and has max_abs 1.56e-7 on near rows, which is above the 1e-12 floor. No anchor-9 clause names this cancellation, and the supplement does not mention pdist.

distance.softdtw.score_rubric_note: Anchor 3 names the softdtw constraint identifiers, which equal softdtw bit for bit in all 32 ident runs. The approved anchor text has no rule for which identifier a unit row describes, so the row was scored on its lowest-scoring identifier. The representative softdtw alone is within max_rel 2.5e-14 of the from-scratch recursion (16/16 runs).
distance.softdtw.score_adjustment_reason: R1: the base identifier softdtw agrees with a from-scratch Cuturi-Blondel Alg. 1 recursion at gamma = 1 in 16/16 runs (max_rel 2.5e-14), and 10 is withheld for the dot-product cancellation that also holds pdist euclidean at 9 (kernel-path +1e4 offset run max_rel 1.008e-8, just above the 1e-8 bar, max_abs 3.0e-7).
distance.softdtw.identifier_exceptions: softdtw_constraint-itakura=3 (wrong): constraint never passed to tslearn, bit-identical to softdtw in 16/16 ident runs (32 for the two constraint identifiers; tests/README bug 3) | softdtw_constraint-sakoe-chiba=3 (wrong): constraint never passed to tslearn, bit-identical to softdtw in 16/16 ident runs (tests/README bug 3)

infotheory.cce.gaussian.score_rubric_note: Anchor 7 fits only in part: the code is the supplement's finite-history sum, but with n = 5 where the supplement says 10 (n10 probe on var2_bivariate T1024 gives 11.95 vs 6.12). Anchor 8 fails because the n = 5 truncation is not a constant-factor or monotone map of the canonical whole-past value.

infotheory.cce.kernel.score_rubric_note: Anchor 7 fits only in part: the code is the supplement's finite-history sum, but with n = 5 where the supplement says 10 (var2_bivariate T1024: n = 10 gives 4.379 / 4.655 vs n = 5 4.384 / 4.659). Anchor 8 fails because the n = 5 truncation is not a constant-factor or monotone map of the canonical whole-past value.

infotheory.cce.kozachenko.score_rubric_note: Anchor 7 fits only in part: the code is the supplement's finite-history sum, but with n = 5 where the supplement says 10 (var2_bivariate T1024: n = 10 gives 12.97 / 13.95 vs n = 5 6.21 / 6.71, run n10-jrand). Anchor 8 fails because the n = 5 truncation is not a constant-factor or monotone map of the canonical whole-past value.

infotheory.ce.gaussian.score_rubric_note: Anchor 9 ddof clause: ddof=1 plug-in covariance. The numpy reference agrees on 6/6 exact runs, max_abs 3.6e-15.

infotheory.ce.kernel.score_rubric_note: Anchor 9 ddof and log-base clauses: N-1 SD z-scoring under the 0.5 SD box, output in bits. The numpy reference agrees on 10/10 exact runs, max_abs 3.0e-14.

infotheory.ce.kozachenko.score_rubric_note: Anchor 10's fp clause fails against canonical KL without jitter: kl runs reach max_abs 1.4e-4 (d = 1 marginal term, ce|var2_bivariate|1024|pipeline|kl). The 1.7e-14 agreement (jrand, 5/5) includes JIDT's seeded 1e-8 jitter, which no anchor-9 clause names.

infotheory.di.gaussian.score_rubric_note: Anchor 4 names DI with block-entropy rate. pyspi equals Massey DI_5 plus the target block term B to 8.9e-16 on var2_bivariate T1024 (0.7746 vs Massey 0.6483).

infotheory.di.kernel.score_rubric_note: Anchor 4 names DI with block-entropy rate. pyspi equals box-kernel Massey DI_5 plus B(target) to 6.7e-14. Estimator bias sets the magnitude: 5.3-5.8 bits on independent white pairs, where the population value is 0.

infotheory.di.kozachenko.score_rubric_note: Anchor 4 names DI with block-entropy rate. pyspi equals Massey DI_5 plus B(target) to 3.7e-14 on var2_bivariate T1024 (0.614 vs Massey 0.449).

infotheory.est.gaussian.score_rubric_note: Anchor 9 ddof clause: entropies use the n-1 covariance (a ddof=0 covariance differs by up to 0.0199 nats at T=256); 72 direct JIDT calls agree with numpy closed forms to max_abs 5.5e-15.

infotheory.est.kernel.score_rubric_note: Anchor 9 ddof and log-base clauses: the box half-width (the Kantz-Schreiber radius r) is W x the N-1 SD and output is in bits (a ddof=0 width differs by 0.0287 bits); direct JIDT vs numpy box kernel max_abs 2.6e-13.

infotheory.est.kozachenko.score_rubric_note: Anchor 1: above 2000 rows JIDT's naive routine returns distances shorter than the nearest-neighbour distance, so the output is not the KL estimate (iid d=10, T=4096: 9.82 vs 14.19 nats from the canonical KL reference). At <= 2000 rows it agrees with canonical KL to 7.1e-15 and on its own would rate 9.

infotheory.est.ksg1.score_rubric_note: Anchor 10's canonical-match clause fails on two conventions that no anchor-9 clause names. On tied data the seeded 1e-8 jitter decides the value (logistic_maps T=256 mi 0.2301/0.2270/0.2305 for seeds 42/43/44). Under a Theiler window psi(N) is not adjusted for the excluded points (JIDT TODO). The unit sits at 9, the highest anchor it clears; the from-scratch KSG1 reference agrees to <= 7.1e-15 over 64 runs.

infotheory.je.gaussian.score_rubric_note: Anchor 9 ddof clause: ddof=1 covariance. The numpy reference agrees on 6/6 exact runs, max_abs 3.6e-15.

infotheory.je.kernel.score_rubric_note: Anchor 9 ddof and log-base clauses: N-1 SD z-scoring under the 0.5 SD box, output in bits. The numpy reference agrees on 12/12 exact runs, max_abs 4.1e-14.

infotheory.je.kozachenko.score_rubric_note: Anchor 10's fp clause fails against canonical KL without jitter: kl runs reach max_abs 1.3e-7 (5.5e-8 relative on je|anm|1024|pipeline|kl). The 1.2e-14 agreement (jrand, 6/6) includes JIDT's seeded 1e-8 jitter, which no anchor-9 clause names.

infotheory.mi.gaussian.score_rubric_note: Agrees with the numpy closed form to max_abs 1.6e-16 (var2_bivariate T=1024); the 'nonlinear' keyword and JIDT version are metadata.

infotheory.mi.kernel.score_rubric_note: Anchor 9 ddof and log-base clauses: widths are 0.25 x each column's N-1 SD, output in bits; 10/10 exact runs agree with the numpy box kernel to <= 1.6e-15.

infotheory.mi.kraskov.score_rubric_note: 7/7 runs agree with the from-scratch KSG1 to <= 4.4e-15 and with sklearn to 0.0-1.3e-15; the 'unsigned' label and JIDT version are metadata.

infotheory.mi.kraskov_DCE.score_rubric_note: Anchor 6: the KSG part agrees to <= 7.1e-15 for W 1-339, but the window comes from the int(Bartlett + 1) all-lag rule, not the documented heuristic (narrowband T=1024: 1.442 without DCE, 2.254 with W=339).

infotheory.phi.Geo_norm-0.score_rubric_note: Anchor 7 fails on both clauses. The PhiToolbox augmented Lagrangian does not pass optimality checks: 24/37 geo-details runs pass, delayed_noise T64 stops with an Eq. 19 residual of 8.2e-3, and shared_envelope T64 is 1.107 nats above the global minimum. Its match to the PhiToolbox the supplement cites rests only on the same-lineage Octave run (16/16, max_abs 3.4e-10), which the README caps at 6; that cap also keeps anchor 9's MATLAB/author clause out. Anchor 6's 'deviates from the supplement' half does not hold literally, because pyspi reproduces that PhiToolbox, so 6 is the highest anchor cleared.

infotheory.phi.Geo_norm-1.score_rubric_note: Anchor 7 fails. The numerator is the norm-0 augmented Lagrangian value, which does not pass optimality checks: 17/21 indep runs pass, and delayed_noise T64 is 2.28e-3 above the independent value after division. The match to the supplement's PhiToolbox rests only on the same-lineage Octave run (10/10, max_abs 1.9e-10), which is capped at 6. The divisor agrees with the from-scratch one (ratio identity 8/8, max_abs 6.9e-18), and anchor 6's 'deviates from the supplement' half does not hold literally, so 6 is the highest anchor cleared.

infotheory.phi.star_norm-0.score_rubric_note: Anchor 9's statistical-tolerance clause, applied as for distance.hhg and misc.lmfit.BayesianRidge. L-BFGS-B leaves beta at 1.0, so pyspi exceeds the independent brentq optimum by at most 4.65e-8 (narrowband_f0-0.25 T256). That is 5.6e-4 of the smallest Monte Carlo SD of the estimator (8.3e-5). Anchor 10 fails because the relative gap reaches 6.4e-4 (iid_gaussian T1024 pair (2,3)). The Octave run uses pyspi's vendored copy and is same-lineage, so the MATLAB/author clause is not used.

infotheory.si.gaussian.score_rubric_note: The numpy reference agrees on 4/4 exact runs, max_abs 8.9e-16. The supplement's reversed term order is a prose-order difference only.

infotheory.si.kernel.score_rubric_note: Anchor 9 ddof and log-base clauses: N-1 SD z-scoring under the 0.5 SD box, output in bits. The numpy reference agrees on 7/7 exact runs, max_abs 7.4e-14.

infotheory.si.kozachenko.score_rubric_note: Anchor 10's fp clause fails against canonical KL without jitter: at T <= 1024, kl runs reach max_abs 2.7e-4 (logistic_maps_bidir). That defect is scored under infotheory.est.kozachenko, and the gap is small against the estimator SD of 0.058 at T4096.

infotheory.te.gaussian_auto-MAX_CORR_AIS.score_rubric_note: Anchor 8 fails because the per-pair AIS embedding search is not a monotone transform of canonical Gaussian TE (var2_bivariate x0 gets k = 3, 10, 9, 8 at T = 64 to 4096). infotheory.te.kraskov_DCE_auto-MAX_CORR_.score_rubric_note: KSG1 TE agrees with the reference on 8/8 runs (<= 2.2e-15) and the AIS embeddings on 5/5 runs. infotheory.te.kraskov_DCE_k-2_kt-1_l-1_l.score_rubric_note: KSG1 TE with k=2 agrees with the reference on 7/7 runs (<= 1.1e-15). The value is set by pyspi's int(Bartlett + 1) all-lag window, which deviates from both the supplement heuristic and canonical practice (infotheory.theiler_window).
